originalTitle: Australia news live: Jacinta Allan urges women not to be discouraged from politics as she quits as Victorian premier; fuel excise cut extension ruled out
content: Sources say Kilkenny making play for Victorian leadership, but could be effort to snag deputy role Sources in Labor’s caucus meeting currently under way say the meeting is taking longer than expected as attorney general Sonya Kilkenny had nominated for leadership against Ben Carroll. However, one source has interpreted the move as a play for the deputy role, which several MPs have said was being eyed by Gabrielle Williams. Kilkenny and Williams are both from the left faction, but the former is a supporter of Allan while Williams was among a grouping within her faction to break ranks to support Carroll. Two MPs have noted that Kilkenny’s move is the very same Carroll used on Daniel Andrews back in 2023 to secure the deputy role. More on that here: Canavan welcomes oil refinery scoping study, but calls for safeguard mechanism to be scrapped Matt Canavan says he’d “love” to see a new oil refinery built, but perhaps predictably, says it can’t be done unless the government scraps its “carbon taxes”. By carbon taxes he means the safeguard mechanism that requires big greenhouse gas emitters to reduce their emissions and offset any excess emissions over a set limit. The scheme was created by the former Coalition government but ratcheted up by Labor. Canavan told News 24 earlier this morning the two remaining refineries in Australia will pay more than $100m in “carbon tax fees by the end of this decade”. I’d love to see a new oil refinery built, but to do that, we’ve got to get rid of Labor’s carbon taxes. This is not going to happen. We’re not going to get a new oil refinery in this country while this government imposes a massive carbon tax on existing refineries, and new ones would be subject to the same. Canavan says that the current two oil refineries still exist in Australia “thanks to the work Angus Taylor did” as energy minister under the Morrison government. But five oil refineries have closed in Australia since 2012 – four of them under the Coalition’s watch. Allan arrives at last caucus meeting The premier, Jacinta Allan, has arrived to her final caucus meeting as leader to rousing applause. Flanked by her loyal supporters including attorney general Sonya Kilkenny, health minister Harriet Shing, finance minister Steve Dimopoulos and energy minister Lily D’Ambrosio. Her deputy, Ben Carroll, who will now be elected Labor leader unopposed, arrived with Gabrielle Williams, who is being touted for the deputy role, as well as members of both his right faction and Allan’s left. Wong rules out extension of fuel excise cut The foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, has ruled out an extension of the fuel excise cut beyond this weekend as petrol and diesel prices surge again amid the war between the US and Israel against Iran. Speaking to ABC Breakfast this morning, Wong said the government would continue to look at ways to relieve households of financial stress but there were no plans to extend the halving of the fuel excise beyond this weekend. What we are focused on is ensuring continued fuel and fertiliser coming into Australia, and we are calling, as so many in the international community are, for there to be ceasefire negotiations and an end to this conflict, which has caused so much global turmoil … Currently, the plan is for the fuel excise to step down. As you know, it’s come down, it’s halved, and the intention is for that to discontinue as of this weekend. The federal government announced a three-month halving of the fuel excise from April, slashing the 52.6c a litre tax temporarily to 26.4c a litre. It is set to expire on 2 August. The news comes as the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, visits Karratha in Western Australia’s Pilbara region to announce a $4m early stage feasibility study into the construction of what would be Australia’s first new oil refinery in 60 years. Read more: Allan says her endometriosis and childbirth experience ‘defined what I believe government should do for working women’ A bit more about Allan’s comments on women’s health, and her time as a female political leader: “I have lived with endometriosis and I almost lost my daughter at birth,” she told assembled media as she announced her resignation as premier just earlier. These experiences not only defined who I am, they defined what I believe government should do for working women. She went on to list some of her government’s achievements: Opening 15 women’s health clinics across the state. Rolling out the green whistle for free pain relief. Access to the contraceptive pill at the chemist without having to pay to see a GP. And the country’s first virtual emergency department. If you’re a woman making your start in politics, let me say this to you today: please don’t look at what I have experienced this week and think ‘Stuff that, I don’t want to be involved.’ Look at the support I have experienced over my career and think, ‘I can make a difference here too.’ Allan asks to be remembered for work supporting women and girls Allan said: If I want to be remembered for one thing, it’s this: I led a government … I led a government that listened to girls about their health. … I am proud to be Victoria’s second female premier, and there have absolutely been moments when it’s been hard and it’s been personal. But the chance to make a difference was worth it … If you want to make a difference in politics, you have to get up and fight and I am a fighter. I have always fought for my family’s Labor values. She said she was “more than ready” to fight again in November, issuing a warning on One Nation’s surge in the state. That remains the biggest risk at this election, a One Nation-Liberal coalition government that will cut $40bn from our hospitals and from our schools. Allan ‘proud’ of building up regional Victoria Allan is listing a string of achievements and her love of Melbourne and regional Victoria: Melbourne’s a great city. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚新闻直播：杰辛塔·艾伦 (Jacinta Allan) 辞去维多利亚州总理职务后，敦促女性不要灰心从政；燃油消费税削减延期被排除
chineseContent: 消息人士称，基尔肯尼正在为维多利亚州的领导层发挥作用，但可能会努力争夺副手角色。目前正在进行的工党核心会议的消息人士称，由于总检察长索尼娅·基尔肯尼提名了本·卡罗尔的领导权，因此会议的时间比预期要长。然而，一位消息人士将此举解读为对副手角色的争夺，几名议员表示加布里埃尔·威廉姆斯正在关注这一职位。基尔肯尼和威廉姆斯都来自左翼派系，但前者是艾伦的支持者，而威廉姆斯是她派系内打破阵营支持卡罗尔的团体之一。两名议员指出，基尔肯尼的举动与卡罗尔在 2023 年为确保副手职位而对丹尼尔·安德鲁斯采取的行动完全相同。更多相关内容：卡纳万欢迎炼油厂范围研究，但呼吁废除保障机制马特·卡纳万表示，他“希望”看到一座新炼油厂的建成，但也许可以预见的是，他表示除非政府取消“碳税”，否则这是不可能的。他所说的碳税是指一种保障机制，要求温室气体排放大国减少排放并抵消超过一定限度的超额排放。该计划由前联合政府制定，但由工党加强。 Canavan 今天早些时候告诉 News 24，澳大利亚剩余的两家炼油厂“到本十年末”将支付超过 1 亿美元的碳税。我很高兴看到一座新的炼油厂建成，但要做到这一点，我们必须取消工党的碳税。这不会发生。当政府对现有炼油厂征收巨额碳税时，我们不会在这个国家建立新的炼油厂，新炼油厂也将受到同样的影响。卡纳万表示，澳大利亚目前仍存在两座炼油厂
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
